newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Kredietbank CEO plays down merger talk. [CORRECTED 08:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Belgian Kredietbank CEO plays down merger talk. [CORRECTED 08:50 GMT]

text.p: Kredietbank Chief Executive officer Marcel Cockaerts on Tuesday played down comments about a possible partner for the Belgian bank by Kredietbank chairman of the board Marc Santens.

"We are always considering major moves on the future of the bank. But at the moment there is not a single dossier (on cooperation or merger) which is ripe for consensus," Cockaerts told Belgian daily De Morgen (corrects paper from De Financieel-Economische Tijd) in an interview.
"I do not want to change our relation with our leading shareholder Almanij, Cockaerts told De Morgen.
In an interview with Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd at the weekend Santens for the first time questioned Kredietbank's long-time independent stance.

"For a long time I said that Kredietbank had no need for an important alliance, but with the formation of a financial Europe, the pressure to look for a larger dimension has increased," he told De Tijd.
"If there is a good scenario, the family shareholders are willing to support it, even if they are diluted," he said.
Kredietbank is 41 percent owned by holding company Almanij, itself largely family owned.

"Our family shareholder structure is an asset, but I admit that in the medium term it may be untenable," Santens said. Santens hinted that Cockaerts could soon be succeeded as CEO by KB director Remi Vermeiren.
Cockaerts told De Morgen he might retire at the end of 1997, April 1998 or the end of 1998 but added that no decision had been taken about a successor.
